declared_scope_description: Technical acceptance verification for M1-M6 on controlled synthetic OSM node_only fixtures and synthetic approved boundaries using real PostgreSQL 16 / PostGIS 3.4 and Alembic revision 0004_m3_staging_immutability. Authoritative post-2025 Ho Chi Minh City publication remains explicitly outside this scope.

tracked_fixtures.description: Controlled M2 synthetic OSM XML fixture covering all 5 approved categories, unnamed/named ATMs, unsupported tags, invalid/ambiguous nodes, and ignored Way element.

source_traceability_notes: docs/ACCEPTANCE_POLICY.md §2 defines exact approved scenario membership counts across four core scopes (Fault Injection & Recovery: 18, Unique Constraints & Idempotency: 26, Cross-table Integrity & Recovery: 28, Migration & Schema: 15; combined total = 87) and mandates additional coverage for column validation, JSONB, spatial correctness, and independently verified geographic fixtures.

Gap recorded per policy: the upstream design prose listing individual scenario titles for the 87 memberships is summarized in docs/ACCEPTANCE_POLICY.md rather than committed verbatim in this repository. Every scenario in this registry is therefore grounded strictly in approved requirements from docs/ARCHITECTURE_BASELINE.md, docs/ACCEPTANCE_POLICY.md, docs/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md, and README.md, and mapped only to tests/gates whose actual assertions prove the expected outcome.

Documentation discrepancy noted: docs/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md and docs/ACCEPTANCE_POLICY.md pre-M6 still displayed M5 awaiting sign-off / implementation verification NOT STARTED, whereas M5 was committed at 2aefa1747fadde707690e718b0d8888887b38c7f after the project owner confirmed 473 passed (1 Starlette TestClient deprecation warning) and authorized M6. Formal IMPLEMENTATION_ACCEPTED sign-off remains reserved for explicit project-owner review.

applicability_rules.description: Downgrading 0001_m1_initial_schema -> base or 0002_m2_staging_tables -> 0001_m1_initial_schema on populated tables is intentionally non-reversible and fails closed with RuntimeError to prevent silent destruction of canonical POI/audit or staging data. Approved recovery/roll-forward alternative: roll-forward Alembic migration or M5 controlled recovery from an immutable verified recovery artifact.

suites.name: S1 — Unit
suites.coverage: Pure Python rules, normalization, validation, classification, guards, and acceptance evaluation

suites.name: S2 — Database Integration
suites.coverage: Real PostgreSQL/PostGIS constraints, staging integration, spatial queries, and API query endpoints

suites.name: S3 — Migration
suites.coverage: Alembic G1-G6 migration lifecycle, catalog contract, drift, and PostGIS reflection checks

suites.name: S4 — Workflow
suites.coverage: Publication, controlled recovery, durable evidence, history, and duplicate-candidate workflows

suites.name: S5 — Race & Fault Injection
suites.coverage: Independent connections, deterministic checkpoints, rollback, concurrency, and reader snapshot isolation

migration_gates.name: G1 — Clean Upgrade
migration_gates.required_check: Upgrade a fresh disposable PostgreSQL/PostGIS database to Alembic head, verify idempotent re-upgrade and exact applied revision.

migration_gates.name: G2 — Schema Contract Verification
migration_gates.required_check: Compare live PostgreSQL catalog tables, spatial column types, validated constraints (convalidated=true), ON DELETE RESTRICT foreign keys, and M3/M3.7 guard triggers against approved contract.

migration_gates.name: G3 — Schema Drift Detection
migration_gates.required_check: Verify zero Alembic/SQLAlchemy drift on cleanly upgraded database and confirm deliberate out-of-band DDL and spatial SRID drift are detected.

migration_gates.name: G4 — Existing-data Compatibility
migration_gates.required_check: Upgrade from earlier revision 0001_m1_initial_schema to head with representative historical data; verify valid rows survive intact and incompatible existing rows fail stricter constraints cleanly without silent repair.

migration_gates.name: G5 — Migration Failure Safety
migration_gates.required_check: Verify failed Alembic upgrade and failed transactional DDL report failure accurately, roll back atomically, and leave alembic_version and database state uncorrupted.

migration_gates.name: G6 — Conditional Downgrade/Re-upgrade
migration_gates.required_check: Verify clean downgrade and re-upgrade on empty DB and non-destructive trigger migrations, verify fail-closed refusal on populated 0001/0002 tables, and record approved roll-forward/recovery alternative.

cases.scenario: Pre-COMMIT publication fault at checkpoint 1 (on_before_lock) rolls back atomically, preserves active V1, and allows idempotent retry with the same UUID.
Pre-COMMIT publication fault at checkpoint 2 (on_after_lock) rolls back atomically, preserves active V1, and allows idempotent retry with the same UUID.
Pre-COMMIT publication fault at checkpoint 3 (on_after_revalidation) rolls back atomically, preserves active V1, and allows idempotent retry with the same UUID.
Pre-COMMIT publication fault at checkpoint 4 (on_before_upsert) rolls back atomically, preserves active V1, and allows idempotent retry with the same UUID.
Pre-COMMIT publication fault at checkpoint 5 (on_during_upsert mid-batch) rolls back partial UPSERT writes atomically and allows idempotent retry.
Pre-COMMIT publication fault at checkpoint 6 (on_after_upsert) rolls back atomically, preserves active V1, and allows idempotent retry.
Pre-COMMIT publication fault at checkpoint 7 (on_during_reconciliation) rolls back atomically, preserves active V1, and allows idempotent retry.
Pre-COMMIT publication fault at checkpoint 8 (on_after_deactivation) rolls back soft-deactivations atomically and preserves active V1.
Pre-COMMIT publication fault at checkpoint 9 (on_during_duplicate_resolution) rolls back duplicate inserts and live mutations atomically.
Pre-COMMIT publication fault at checkpoint 10 (on_during_pre_commit_verification) rolls back atomically and preserves active V1.
Pre-COMMIT publication fault at checkpoint 11 (on_during_active_slot_switch) rolls back active-slot switch atomically and preserves V1.
Pre-COMMIT publication fault at checkpoint 12 (on_before_commit) rolls back all live writes atomically and allows safe retry.
Post-COMMIT lost ACK fault at checkpoint 13 (on_after_commit_before_ack) keeps committed V2 durable; durable evidence inspection + retry returns ALREADY_PUBLISHED without re-applying.
Lost COMMIT ACK followed by V3 supersession: retrying V2 with original operation UUID returns ALREADY_PUBLISHED without reactivating superseded V2.
Mid-run staging batch failure, corrupt OSM stream, and mid-stream truncated XML roll back failed batches atomically and block PREPARED readiness.
Controlled recovery pre-COMMIT fault injection across all 14 preparation and publication checkpoints rolls back cleanly and leaves active V2 intact.
Controlled recovery lost COMMIT ACK resolves via durable operation evidence; retry after completion or subsequent supersession returns ALREADY_PUBLISHED without re-applying.
API gracefully degrades under database unavailability (503), bounded statement timeout (504), and unexpected failures (500) without leaking credentials, SQL, or connection pool leases.
places enforces UNIQUE(osm_type, osm_id) and rejects duplicate OSM identities with SQLSTATE 23505.
places allows identical numeric osm_id values across distinct osm_type values (node, way, relation).
places.id remains stable across UPSERT updates, soft-deactivation, and subsequent reactivation in V1 -> V2 -> V3 publications.
PostgreSQL trigger trg_places_identity_guard blocks mutating places.id, osm_type, osm_id, or created_at on existing rows.
boundary_versions enforces unique version_code (uq_boundary_versions_version_code) and rejects duplicates with SQLSTATE 23505.
import_runs does not treat source_fingerprint as unique; re-importing the same source creates distinct independent run IDs.
Source fingerprints and candidate content digests are deterministic and sensitive to source snapshot, boundary, pipeline, normalizer, and config inputs.
Guarded staging resume rejects mismatched source_fingerprint and refuses reusing an already-published run.
Guarded staging resume rejects mismatched source_checksum_sha256 for an in-progress PROCESSING run.
Staging refuses returning PREPARED, PUBLISHED, SUPERSEDED, FAILED, or ABORTED runs to PROCESSING.
staging_place_candidates enforces unique (import_run_id, osm_type, osm_id) within a run while isolating identical OSM identities across independent runs.
Staging retry on identical input is idempotent without duplicating rows or inflating counters; conflicting duplicate OSM identity is quarantined without overwriting and blocks readiness.
Idempotent staging_issue_fingerprints deduplicates identical nullable-OSM-identity issues on retry without merging distinct malformed occurrences.
import_runs enforces unique non-null publication_operation_id while permitting multiple NULL rows for unpublished runs.
Nil publication UUID is rejected, conflicting UUID ownership across runs is blocked, and registered publication_operation_id is immutable at DB trigger level.
uq_import_runs_active_slot allows zero or one active publication slot (active_slot=1) and rejects a second simultaneous active publication.
Publication retry handles Cases A (pre-commit retry), B (post-commit idempotent return), C (lost ACK resolution), and D (conflicting UUID rejection) safely.
Conflicting operation UUID registration fails before pre-publication recovery artifact export so zero orphan artifacts are written.
Two concurrent workers publishing the same prepared run with the same operation UUID: exactly one commits and the other receives ALREADY_PUBLISHED.
Two concurrent workers racing with independent operation UUIDs on the same prepared run: one wins registration and the other fails with PublicationConflictError.
Two concurrent workers publishing different runs against the same V1 baseline: winner commits and loser fails closed under advisory lock, preventing stale overwrites.
Two concurrent workers attempting to reuse the same operation UUID on two different prepared runs: only one succeeds and the second is rejected.
duplicate_candidates enforces canonical pair order (place_a_id < place_b_id), per-run uniqueness UNIQUE(import_run_id, place_a_id, place_b_id), and cross-run coexistence.
Duplicate candidate resolution canonicalizes pairs, is retry-idempotent without overwriting immutable evidence, preserves historical rows across deactivation, and never auto-merges POIs.
Controlled recovery operation UUID is idempotent on replay, rejects repurposing for a different artifact or approval, and never reactivates a superseded recovery run.
Controlled recovery stale approval expecting V2 is rejected under pg_advisory_xact_lock when concurrent V3 commits first.
import_runs CHECK constraints enforce active_slot=1 iff status=PUBLISHED and require publication_operation_id, published_at, and superseded_at lifecycle consistency.
Transitioning PUBLISHED -> SUPERSEDED across real COMMIT retains durable publication_operation_id, published_at, superseded_at, and publication_evidence.
Foreign keys use ON DELETE RESTRICT to protect boundary_versions, import_runs, and places from destructive cascading deletes.
Trigger trg_boundary_versions_guard enforces immutable geometry/provenance and monotonic DRAFT -> VALIDATED -> APPROVED lifecycle.
Trigger trg_import_runs_guard enforces APPROVED boundary for PUBLISHED runs and prevents in-place evidence mutation or key stripping on PUBLISHED -> SUPERSEDED.
0004 triggers block direct INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on staging tables and import_issues once parent run is PREPARED, PUBLISHED, or SUPERSEDED.
Concurrent staging writers racing with verify_and_prepare_run serialize on row/share locks and fail closed rather than slipping unverified rows into PREPARED runs.
Tampered staging digests or concurrent staging mutations during open publication are caught under lock and roll back publication without reader leakage.
Source file modification, replacement, or clean truncation between checksum verification and parsing fails closed with SOURCE_INTEGRITY_ERROR.
Staging readiness fails closed on mismatched boundary_version_id, unfiltered out-of-boundary rows, empty staging, stale/extra rows, tampered counts, or unverified post-parse state.
Default AUTHORITATIVE publication mode rejects incomplete node_only runs; DRAFT and VALIDATED boundaries are blocked while APPROVED synthetic boundary passes CONTROLLED_TEST_NODE_ONLY.
Incomplete node_only runs cannot replace an active full-coverage dataset, and non-PREPARED run statuses fail publication preflight.
AUTHORITATIVE mode rejects synthetic boundary evidence; first publication rejects orphaned active Node/Way/Relation places; CONTROLLED_TEST_NODE_ONLY fails closed on dev/non-test DBs.

Atomic publication enforces active OSM identities == prepared canonical OSM identities, updates last_seen_import_id even on unchanged places, soft-deactivates absent identities without hard delete, and preserves non-node scopes cleanly.
Pre-commit verification rejects unexpected pre-existing duplicate_candidates rows across NOT_EXECUTED, VERIFIED_EMPTY, and CANDIDATES_PROVIDED states.
First publication with zero prior active run returns None from prepare_recovery_artifact and rejects any unexpectedly supplied recovery artifact.
Immutable recovery artifact captures complete canonical places, provenance, manifest, and checksums, rejects tampering/corruption, and prevents overwriting existing artifact directories.
Recovery artifact reads one REPEATABLE READ snapshot and live-baseline verification rejects post-snapshot place content drift, duplicate pair/evidence drift, and boundary EWKB/provenance drift.
Controlled recovery rejects missing, tampered, unsupported format, or provenance-mismatched historical source artifacts fail-closed without mutating live data.
Controlled recovery requires a valid, timezone-aware, non-blank, cryptographically bound manual RecoveryApproval and rejects missing/malformed/mismatched approvals fail-closed.

Controlled recovery restores exact V1 canonical content, membership, active boundary, stable places.id, and last_seen_import_id via a new RECOVERY run while keeping V1 source and V2 protection artifacts distinct and preserving all history.

Default controlled recovery records duplicate_detection_state=NOT_EXECUTED without copying V1/V2 duplicate rows or falsely reporting VERIFIED_EMPTY, while retaining historical duplicate rows on original runs.
Database-level readers using READ COMMITTED single-statement and REPEATABLE READ READ ONLY multi-query helpers observe consistent committed snapshots during atomic and rolled-back publications.
Concurrent FastAPI readers never observe uncommitted V2 publication writes, see atomic switch upon COMMIT, and never observe rolled-back V3 writes.
FastAPI multi-query endpoints (/api/v1/places and /api/v1/places/nearby) execute COUNT(*) and SELECT inside one REPEATABLE READ READ ONLY transaction and never mix V1 total with V2 items.
FastAPI enforces PostgreSQL READ ONLY isolation levels, rejects non-GET write verbs (405), hides unpublished PREPARED staging runs, and hides orphan active places when no active_slot=1 exists.
Concurrent FastAPI readers do not observe uncommitted controlled-recovery writes and never mix V2 total with recovered V1 items across COMMIT.
Fail-closed database guards isolate TEST_DATABASE_URL from DATABASE_URL, reject unsafe/non-test/remote URLs and loopback aliases, and prevent API fallback to TEST_DATABASE_URL.
G1: Clean Alembic upgrade to head (0004_m3_staging_immutability) succeeds on a fresh PostgreSQL/PostGIS database and records exact applied revision.
G1: Re-running Alembic upgrade head when already at head is a safe idempotent no-op.
G1/Core packaging: Alembic upgrade, current, and check succeed in a core-only installation without optional python-dotenv.
G2: PostgreSQL catalog contains exactly the five approved canonical business tables plus the three M2 technical staging tables, with zero unauthorized extra tables.
G2: PostgreSQL catalog confirms exact spatial column types geometry(MultiPolygon,4326) on boundary_versions.geom and geography(Point,4326) on places.location and staging_place_candidates.location.
G2: Every required PK, UNIQUE, CHECK, and ON DELETE RESTRICT FK constraint is present in pg_constraint with convalidated=true.
G2: All 8 approved M3/M3.7 guard triggers are installed in pg_trigger across canonical and technical staging tables.
G3: Cleanly upgraded database produces zero Alembic/SQLAlchemy metadata drift, and out-of-band DDL column additions are detected as drift.
G3: Custom PostGIS SQLAlchemy reflection distinguishes SRID 0, 3857, and 4326 and detects spatial SRID drift.
G3: PostGIS/tiger extension-managed tables are excluded without hiding public user tables with colliding names, and autogenerate renders executable PostGIS type imports.
G4: Upgrading from earlier revision 0001_m1_initial_schema to head with representative historical canonical rows preserves all valid data intact and activates M3/M3.7 guard triggers.
G4: Introducing a stricter constraint incompatible with existing rows fails cleanly with SQLSTATE 23514 without silently repairing or destroying legacy data.
G5: Failed Alembic migration and failed transactional DDL report failure accurately, roll back atomically, and leave alembic_version and database schema uncorrupted.
G6: Empty-DB downgrade (head -> base -> head) and populated non-destructive trigger downgrade/re-upgrade (0004 -> 0002 -> head) succeed cleanly with zero schema drift.

G6: Populated destructive downgrades (0002 -> 0001 with staging rows; 0001 -> base with canonical rows) fail closed preserving revision and data; destructive downgrade on populated data is non-reversible under approved roll-forward/controlled-recovery rule G6_POPULATED_DESTRUCTIVE_DOWNGRADE.

Approved five-category domain (cafe, restaurant, atm, pharmacy, supermarket) enforced deterministically in Python classification, PostgreSQL CHECK constraints, and API filters; conflicting multi-category tags quarantined.

Name nullability enforced consistently: ATM allows NULL name + NULL name_search without fabricating placeholders; non-ATM requires non-blank name; blank/malformed names rejected at Python and SQL layers.
Vietnamese name_search normalization applies Unicode casefolding, combining-mark removal, đ/Đ -> d, whitespace normalization, invisible Cf removal, and NFC/NFD parity.
Address is optional and never fabricated; blank addresses normalize to NULL in Python and are rejected directly by PostgreSQL CHECK.

raw_tags and all JSONB metadata columns (import_runs, import_issues, duplicate_candidates, boundary_versions) enforce JSON object type and preserve original decoded OSM tags without mixing provenance.
OSM identity domain (node/way/relation), positive osm_id, required NOT NULL columns, paired import_issues OSM identity, and OSM version/changeset/timestamp metadata are enforced.

boundary_versions row-level CHECK constraints enforce DRAFT -> VALIDATED -> APPROVED statuses, per-state metadata completeness, SHA-256 checksum format, and valid non-empty SRID 4326 MultiPolygon geometry.

Streaming Pyosmium Node-only extractor deterministically processes XML and binary .osm.pbf fixtures, quarantines invalid records, computes reproducible file checksums, and enforces PostgreSQL staging CHECK constraints.

cases.requirement_ref: docs/ARCHITECTURE_BASELINE.md §3; docs/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md M4; README.md API Contract
cases.scenario: FastAPI input validation rejects malformed coordinates, radius, pagination, IDs, oversized/NUL queries, and unsupported categories with HTTP 422 before hitting the database.

M6 Acceptance Registry validator and evidence evaluator fail closed on missing evidence, failed/skipped/xfailed blocking tests, malformed artifacts, stale commit SHAs, and secret leaks, while preserving rerun failure history.
WGS84 coordinate finiteness and bounds (lon in [-180,180], lat in [-90,90]) and ST_MakePoint(longitude, latitude) ordering are enforced in Python and PostgreSQL.
PostGIS extension is available and executes point construction, geography distance, and ST_Covers on the dedicated test database.

ST_Covers on synthetic MultiPolygon with hole and island accurately classifies interior, outer boundary edge, outer vertex, hole interior, hole boundary edge, island interior, island boundary edge, and outside points.
End-to-end staging ingestion and atomic publication enforce ST_Covers membership across complex MultiPolygon boundaries (interior, edges, vertices, holes, islands, outside).
GET /health verifies PostgreSQL readiness without mutating DB state and registers OpenAPI schema.
GET /api/v1/places/{id} returns active canonical place details (including unnamed ATM nulls), excludes internal columns, and returns 404 for inactive or staging-only rows.
GET /api/v1/places performs Vietnamese-normalized search, literal LIKE wildcard/backslash escaping, 5-category filtering, and deterministic pagination on real PostgreSQL.

GET /api/v1/places/nearby computes PostGIS WGS84 spheroidal ST_DWithin/ST_Distance in meters, distinguishes geodesic meters from planar degrees, enforces exact radius boundary equality, and sorts closest-first with deterministic id tie-break.
Staging persists validated candidates with exact PostGIS geography(Point,4326) representation and passes full readiness verification.
Independently verified post-2025 Ho Chi Minh City administrative boundary (including former Binh Duong, former Ba Ria-Vung Tau, and Con Dao) and independently verified geographic reference points.
cases.deferral_rationale: External authoritative post-2025 HCMC boundary polygon and independently verified geographic reference coordinates (including Con Dao) have not been supplied; synthetic fixtures are explicitly prohibited from being treated as authoritative. M3 safeguards block AUTHORITATIVE publication until verified.

cases.scenario: Full OSM Way and Relation geometry extraction (beyond M2 Node-only streaming extraction).
cases.deferral_rationale: Ways and Relations are explicitly deferred to a later incremental milestone; M3 eligibility guards fail closed and block AUTHORITATIVE publication for node_only runs.

cases.scenario: Automated heuristic duplicate-candidate matching thresholds (distance, name similarity, and scoring rules).
cases.deferral_rationale: Approved M5 Option 2 + Option A scope defers automated heuristic matching until formal distance/name-matching/scoring rules are approved; canonical pair ordering, uniqueness, immutability, historical retention, NOT_EXECUTED default, and no auto-merge are verified.

cases.scenario: Dedicated search and spatial indexing optimization strategy (GIST, GIN, trigram, partial indexes).
cases.deferral_rationale: Explicitly out of scope until an indexing optimization strategy is separately reviewed and approved.

cases.scenario: Production deployment, multi-city publication, scaling, and production chaos infrastructure.
cases.deferral_rationale: Explicitly out of scope for the current MVP backend and database integrity milestone.
